paragraphs: A forestry machine seat is a workstation. The operator spends the shift turning, looking up at a boom and working two joysticks, so the seat rotates, the armrests carry the controls, and the whole assembly is suspended against a machine that never sits still.
The model is light at 15,263 polygons and 16,235 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 6 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $59 it suits machinery interior visualisation, equipment marketing, ergonomics and training material, cab scenes, film props and game environments. On sale since 2020.

The flatbed is the oldest trailer type still in wide use because it puts no limit on the shape of the load. Everything is strapped or chained down in the open, which makes securing the cargo a trade in its own right rather than a matter of shutting a door.

The model holds 137,424 polygons and 139,612 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 8 maps, 7 at 4096x4096 and one at 1024x1024. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a generic build is offered separately.
At $59 it suits logistics and haulage visualisation, industrial and construction scenes, fleet mockups, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2015.

The floating island is one of the oldest images in fantasy art, and it works because it breaks exactly one rule and leaves everything else intact. Trees, rock and soil behave normally; only the ground underneath is missing.
The scene is supplied in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and is built to CheckMate specification.
At $59 it suits fantasy and game environments, film and animation backgrounds, concept art, book and editorial illustration, and advertising. On sale since 2026.

A floor mill takes the top few millimetres off concrete, which is how a surface gets levelled, a coating gets removed or a slab gets prepared for something new. The drum is full of cutters and the dust extraction is not optional.
The model holds 262,477 polygons and 265,986 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, in blue, and carries StemCell certification.
At $59 it suits construction and renovation visualisation, equipment marketing, training and safety material, site scenes, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2026.

American football gear is regulated down to the millimetre because every piece of it has a rule behind it, usually written after an injury. What looks like a kit list is actually a legal document expressed in plastic and foam.
This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying the equipment as static pieces. It is built to CheckMate specification, and two further volumes of the set are offered separately.
At $59 the set suits sports and equipment visualisation, retail and e-commerce imagery, broadcast graphics, advertising, game characters and editorial illustration. On sale since 2016.

A bottle in ice is a promise about time. It says the drink is ready now, that somebody prepared for this, and that the scene is about to happen rather than being over, which is why the image appears in advertising far more often than a poured glass.
The model holds 32,168 polygons and 31,224 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplying the bottle together with the ice bucket. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $59 it suits food and beverage visualisation, packaging and product imagery, hospitality and event scenes, advertising, film set dressing and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A gold finished display head is retail theatre. It is not trying to look like a person, it is trying to hold a hat or a pair of glasses while being obviously an object, and the metallic finish is what stops the eye reading it as a face.
The model is very light at 5,790 polygons and 5,781 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with hair, and carries StemCell certification.
At $59 it suits retail and window display visualisation, product and accessory presentation, interior scenes, advertising, film set dressing and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

An intermediate coach is the part of a high speed train that repeats. No cab, no power car, just seating between two others, and the whole economics of the train depend on how many of these can be added without changing anything else.
The model holds 550,314 polygons and 582,227 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout, supplied with interior. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $59 it suits rail and transport visualisation, station and infrastructure scenes, interior presentation, advertising, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2026.

Goalie pads are measured to the player, and the rules cap how wide they can be, because the difference between covering the net and covering most of it is the entire game. The flat face is deliberate: a puck should drop, not rebound.
The model holds 139,310 polygons and 144,870 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 12 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $59 it suits sports equipment and retail visualisation, e-commerce imagery, broadcast graphics, advertising, game characters and editorial illustration. On sale since 2016.

A satellite spends the most dangerous part of its life folded. Panels stowed, antennas clamped, everything packed into a fairing, and the entire mission depends on a sequence of hinges that will be used exactly once and cannot be tested in gravity.
The model holds 86,236 polygons and 88,742 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in the folded configuration. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $59 it suits space and technology visualisation, news and documentary graphics, education and museum work, launch sequence animation and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

The keyboard case turned the tablet into an argument about what a laptop is. It floats the screen above the keys on a cantilever, which is structurally silly and works, and it is the reason so many people stopped carrying two devices.

The model is built at subdivision level, 53,629 polygons and 55,897 vertices with non-overlapping UVs, so it smooths cleanly for close product work. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a second build is offered separately.
At $59 it suits product and technology visualisation, screen and interface mockups, office and interior scenes, e-commerce imagery, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2020.

Lacrosse is the oldest organised sport on the continent and its equipment still reflects that: a netted head on a shaft, essentially unchanged in principle, wrapped in modern protection that had to be invented once the game got faster.
This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying the equipment as static pieces. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $59 the set suits sports and equipment visualisation, retail and e-commerce imagery, broadcast graphics, advertising, game characters and editorial illustration. On sale since 2019.

The convention centre loop is a tunnel with cars in it, which is either the future of transit or a very expensive taxi rank depending on who is describing it. Either way the tunnel itself is a striking piece of infrastructure, lit as a feature rather than as a service.
The model is light at 36,453 polygons and 38,245 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.

At $59 it suits infrastructure and transport visualisation, urban and technology presentation, news and documentary graphics, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

The lungs are not symmetrical. The left one has two lobes rather than three, because the heart takes the space, and that asymmetry is one of the first things a student has to stop expecting the body to be tidy about.

The model is light at 15,902 polygons and 15,913 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 5 maps all at 4096x4096, so it runs in interactive and browser based material. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $59 it suits medical education and patient explanation, respiratory and pharmaceutical material, biology teaching, interactive apps and editorial illustration. On sale since 2018.
